From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps - Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet you and Michael earlier. Thanks again for the intro and for walking us through your current fraud-detection pipeline. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align next steps: 

Attendees (today): Sarah Bennett (FinovateBank, Product Lead), Michael Chen (Fraud Ops), Marissa Cole (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE)

Key notes:
- Primary goal: reduce false positives and latency on customer-facing alerts (target 30% reduction in human review)
- Volume: ~2M events/day, median sequence length ~180 tokens for enrichment prompts
- Must-haves: SOC 2 evidence, data retention controls, VPC/private deployment for certain datasets

Immediate asks / checklist: 
1) Stakeholder map: economic buyer (CIO), security head, procurement contact — can you confirm names and emails?
2) Procurement process: any required contract templates, PO timeline, or legal redlines to expect?
3) Security questionnaire: we can provide SOC2 report + security summary; do you have an existing spreadsheet we should complete?
4) Champion enablement: your internal champion said they wanted a one-pager and a technical talk track — attaching a short ROI one-pager for review.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can share the procurement contact and security contact we’ll loop in our Security lead (Evelyn Hart) and SE (Dev) to answer technical/procurement questions.
- Can we schedule a 30–45m procurement + security sync the week of May 17?

Attached: redwood-roi-onepager.pdf (one-pager ROI + pricing framework)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and materials. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side.

Stakeholder map (high-level):
- Tom Lee — CIO (economic buyer) — tom.lee@finovatebank.com
- Priya Malhotra — Head of Security (owns SOC2/controls) — priya.malhotra@finovatebank.com
- Procurement team — procurement@finovatebank.com (primary intake)
- Michael Chen — Fraud Ops (day-to-day owner) — michael.chen@finovatebank.com

Procurement + legal: our procurement team prefers a standard SaaS MSA + SOW; they typically request a 60–90 day review cycle for new vendors. I’ve CC’d procurement so they have visibility.

Security: we do have a security spreadsheet (vendor_security_questionnaire_v2.xlsx). Procurement asked that vendors upload evidence to our secure intake portal; alternately, we can accept a shared link to your SOC2 and a zipped evidence stub. Can Evelyn point us to the SOC2 report and a short mapping doc?

Next steps from our side:
- Procurement asked for a short vendor intake packet (MSA, SOC2 link, contacts) by EOD May 14 if possible.
- OK to schedule a procurement + security sync week of May 17; prefer Tue/Wed morning (CT).

Appreciate the ROI one-pager — that will help the procurement deck.

Best,
Sarah
Product Lead, Fraud Prevention | FinovateBank
